brief: A podcast player where episodes are constellations — listened ones glow, series form patterns

dominant_strengths: Strong metaphor: constellations-as-series creates a memorable, poetic mental model that differentiates from list-based podcast UIs
Cohesive cosmic palette with subtle glow hierarchy (cyan listened, orange playing, dim unplayed) reads instantly
Restrained typography and clean sidebar give the starfield room to breathe and become the hero
dominant_weaknesses: Wayfinding is poor — no episode titles on hover, no labels for which constellation is which series, navigation relies on memory
Massive empty canvas on right-center feels uncomposed; constellations float without anchoring grid or balance
Transport controls are tiny, bottom-left orphaned, and disconnected from the now-playing card visually
fix_priorities: Add hover/tap affordances revealing episode titles and series names directly on stars
Color-code or label constellations to map clearly onto the four sidebar series
Rebalance composition — anchor constellations to implied zones or let user pan, and integrate transport with now-playing panel
Add subtle parallax/twinkle motion to justify the spatial canvas and reward exploration
rationale.norman_balance: Visceral and reflective both sing through the metaphor, but behavioral usability collapses because stars lack labels and the interaction model is unexplained.
rationale.intent_fit: Strongly delivers the constellation-as-episodes concept conceptually, but stops at the visual metaphor without solving how a user actually browses or plays.
